title: Nature's Nectar — Risk & Reputation Research
content:
According to Trustpilot, customers are dissatisfied with Nectar, rating it "Bad" with 1.4/5. Complaints include severe sogginess ruining sleep and back pain, and a mattress that becomes uncomfortable and ripped after a few years. YouTube reviews mention criticism for claiming American manufacturing while being made in China and unclear flame retardant use. NCOA expert reviews highlight edge support issues, lack of support for stomach sleepers, and non-removable covers. Testers noted discomfort for stomach sleepers and edge collapse issues.

this long so had to look at replacing the mattress. Really disappointed with Nectar overall. We are a physically fit couple in our 40’s, both less than 1.8m in height and well within the weight limitations of the mattress. Based on our experience we would never buy from Nectar again or recommend to others. [...] ## Terrible quality and useless "lifetime" warranty—avoid!
Bought a Nectar mattress trusting their lifetime warranty and return promises. Over time, it developed severe sogginess that ruined my sleep and left me with constant back pain. [...] ## Nectar Disappoints
Nectar will void the warranty if you unzip the top cover. The reason: They don't want consumers to see just how ripped it is under the cover. This mattress had become so uncomfortable I unzipped it to see if there was an issue. Although I can't post pictures, take my word for it, it's all ripped and looks terrible. Do yourself a favor and pass on Nectar, after a few years they're uncomfortable, and of course ripped.

## The Classic Memory Foam: Nectar’s Flagship Mattress [...] Testers did caution that anyone who prefers to sleep on their stomach may not feel supported enough on the Nectar Premier Hybrid. “I sink in too much on the stomach position, so my back starts to arch and it feels uncomfortable,” said one tester. A lack of edge support was also noted: Testers gave this mattress a score of only 2/5 for edge support, and one said he didn’t feel secure when seated on the edge of the mattress. [...] Our shorter testers noted that some of the Nectar mattresses, because of their dense foam layers, felt higher than other mattresses they tested.

Testers said that, although the Nectar Classic Hybrid feels stable, they would’ve liked stronger edges. “I feel like the edge collapsed a bit when I was sitting on the edge of the bed,” one tester said. “I had to use my hands to assist myself in getting up and down. I also felt my bottom start to slide a bit because of the topper’s silky texture.”

According to the Better Business Bureau complaints, some customers experienced delivery delays and issues with Nectar Sleep's delivery service, including a driver not returning during the delivery window and a lack of response from the delivery company. Another complaint highlighted a failed white-glove delivery service where the driver arrived early and was rude. On PissedConsumer, complaints included a failed pickup of an order that was shipped against the customer's instructions and poor customer service. Nectar Sleep's FAQ states that standard delivery takes 2-5 business days and white glove delivery typically takes 10-14 business days. The sources do not provide a definitive answer to the current status of delivery delays or service quality issues.

The driver did not return during the delivery window. I contacted the delivery company multiple times without a response and repeatedly contacted Nectar. Nectar said it could not reach its delivery partner or provide any resolution. By the end of the day, the mattress had not been delivered, and I had no information about whether or when it would arrive. [...] I purchased a Nectar mattress with white-glove delivery for my 90-year-old grandfather, who does not speak English and cannot accept the delivery alone. We arranged for someone to be at his home during the confirmed delivery window.  
  The driver arrived more than 30 minutes early. When I explained that someone would be there within 30 minutes and before the scheduled window began, he was rude and hung up. When I called back, he said his supervisor would contact me, but no one ever did. [...] I purchased the mattress and delivery from Nectar. Nectar selected the delivery provider and is responsible for delivering the order as promised. Its inability to manage its vendor should not become the customer’s problem.  
  I am requesting a confirmed delivery date and time window and a refund for the failed white-glove service.

A California federal judge declined to certify nationwide and California classes proposed in the class action lawsuit that alleged Kern’s Nectar juice misled customers into thinking they were free of artificial flavors.
 U.S. District Judge Linda Lopez determined that the plaintiffs, Warren Gross and Deborah Levin, failed to provide “any common evidence” to prove that a class of consumers “would have been deceived by the products’ alleged mislabeling.” [...] The plaintiffs state that, because the Kern’s Nectar juice contains artificial flavor, federal and state laws require that the products display front and back label disclosures that state the product is artificially flavored.

However, the Kern’s Nectar class action lawsuit says the manufacturer of the juice at issue report the products as “100% Natural.” [...] In addition, the plaintiffs state that the ingredient list violates federal and state law because it identifies malic acid only as the generic “malic acid” and not the specific non-generic name of the ingredient.

The Kern’s Nectar juice class action lawsuit also claims that the products contain undisclosed artificial flavoring made from petrochemicals.
